fact: As of the article's date (no other date given), Starlink holds no licence in The Gambia: the Minister of Digital Economy refused to approve the VSAT permit paid for in February 2026, saying Starlink needs a general satellite licence.

As of 18 May 2026 no licence has been issued to Starlink in The Gambia although it paid the fee; the Minister declined to sign a VSAT licence because Starlink says it is not a VSAT, and PURA has recommended approval.

As of 3 March 2026 Starlink says it has not received its final licence in The Gambia, though terms were agreed in November 2024 and fees paid on 2 December 2024; only the Minister's signature is outstanding.

As of 16 February 2026 no Starlink licence has been issued in The Gambia; the Minister had told the National Assembly in July 2025 that PURA recommended approval but he found critical issues needing further review.

On 9 July 2025 the Minister of Digital Economy told the National Assembly that Starlink's VSAT licence recommended by PURA had not been signed because Starlink is not a VSAT, and the application was under reassessment, to go to cabinet.

Agence Ecofin reports Starlink's availability map lists the Gambia among 16 African markets as 'Starting in 2026', shown in the colour meaning coverage or regulatory authorisation pending, with no launch date; service is not yet available there.
MyBroadband's 17 July 2026 table of Starlink status lists Gambia with estimated availability '2026', not 'Available', so no Starlink service on sale in the Gambia.
TechnoMag lists the Gambia among 19 countries 'Scheduled for 2026', not among the countries where Starlink is active, so not on sale as of mid-2026 (article dated 29 June 2026).
